name: skill-authoring
description: How to create, refine or remove a skill in w/skills. Load when teaching yourself a reusable ability or managing one of your own skills.

content.inline:
# Authoring a skill

A skill is a small asset you write to **`w/skills/<name>`** — your own skill
space. Once written it appears in your skills index and you can load it whenever
it's relevant. Skills are reversible: use the delete-skill tool when one should
be removed or a test skill needs cleaning up.

## Shape

- `name` — short kebab-case id, matching the last path segment
- `description` — ONE line: what it does AND when to load it, in the words the
  user actually says (pack in the trigger keywords and their synonyms — e.g. a
  skill about earlier chats should say "past conversation sessions", "what we
  discussed", "history"). This one line is all you see in the index, so it must
  make you reach for the skill at the right moment. Documentation goes in the
  body, never in the description.
- `content.contentType` — `"text/markdown"`
- `content.inline` — the skill body: the actual instructions, in markdown
- `skill` — optional extras: `{ "tools": ["v/ops/..."] }` brings in operations
  while the skill is loaded (full catalogue paths, only the ones the body
  actually teaches); `{ "skills": ["w/skills/other"] }` reveals a sub-skill;
  `{ "skillsets": ["w/skills/recipes"] }` reveals a whole directory of them.
  A `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + markdown) works unchanged.

## Body style

Write for yourself in the middle of a task: concise, imperative, specific.
Name each step by what it does and show the argument or result shape; put a
gotcha where it applies. Aim for 1–2 KB — a loaded body returns every turn.
Never hard-code a tool's callable name in the body (those names are generated
and may change); describe the capability and keep the `v/ops/...` path in
`skill.tools`.

## Create or refine

Use the lattice write tool. For example, to teach yourself the user's email
style, write path `w/skills/email-style` with value:

```json
{
  "name": "email-style",
  "description": "How the user likes emails written. Load when drafting email.",
  "content": { "contentType": "text/markdown",
               "inline": "Keep emails short and warm; sign off with just a first name; ..." },
  "skill": {}
}
```

Then verify it: read it back with the skills-read tool, load it, and check the
load result reports nothing unresolved. From then on it's part of you — load it
when the task calls for it. Keep each skill focused and give it a precise
description.

## Remove

Use the delete-skill tool with the exact skill name, not a path.
